svg.aria-label: Validation and results: the identity sweep, the matched head-to-head with a PPI-Affinity clone, error across datasets, pose accuracy, the published RAPiDock benchmark numbers, predicted versus measured binding energies, and the MDM2 and p53 example.
svg.text: Leave-cluster-out sweep: MAE stays flat while r falls and levels off
925 PDBbind peptide complexes, placement-aware identity metric (30% gives 410 clusters)
Same folds, same complexes: against a PPI-Affinity clone
T100 is PPI-Affinity's own curated set: it wins there, which is why the headline uses matched, leakage-free folds
on PPIKB about 20% of labels are IC50/EC50, which are not thermodynamic
scoring our own poses costs about 0.1 kcal/mol of MAE
median Cα-RMSD to the crystal pose (Å, lower is better)
predictions sit between −9.3 and −9.8 while the
references span −4.8 to −12.7: the range is compressed
Why we compare against RAPiDock: it beats the other tools (re-plotted from Zhao et al., 2025)
Success rates under CAPRI-peptide standards. Numbers are those stated in the text of Zhao et al. (2025); ADCP in iv is derived from the reported gaps (41.1, 33.5 and 20.0 points).
Also reported there: RAPiDock needs 0.35 s per complex, about 270 times faster than AlphaFold2-Multimer, and beats it on DockQ for most complexes.
1. Zhao et al. (2025): RAPiDock beats AlphaFold2-Multimer, AlphaFold3, ADCP, GOLD, HADDOCK, MDockPeP and HPEPDOCK
2. This work: HybriDock-Pep beats RAPiDock on our matched sets (median Cα-RMSD, success rates, cumulative DockQ, Fig. 8)
3. So HybriDock-Pep is ahead of those tools by transitivity; we did not rerun them all on our sets
the only tools we ran ourselves: RAPiDock, ADCP, Boltz-2 and ESMFold (one pose each for the two co-folding tools)
Example: MDM2 and the p53 peptide (PDB 1YCR)
kcal/mol; Kd of the p53 peptide is about 0.6 µM
